item.text: I’ll perform the smoke test locally in the current directory, then verify both outputs and their exact contents.

item.command:
/usr/bin/bash -lc "pwd && python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import openpyxl

root = Path.cwd()
source = root / \"input\" / \"toy.txt\"
out_dir = root / \"output\"
out_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
text = source.read_text()

book = openpyxl.Workbook()
sheet = book.active
sheet.title = \"Smoke\"
sheet[\"A1\"] = \"sandbox-ok\"
sheet[\"A2\"] = text
book.save(out_dir / \"smoke.xlsx\")

(out_dir / \"result.txt\").write_text(f\"OK\\n{openpyxl.__version__}\\n\")
print(openpyxl.__version__)
PY
python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import openpyxl

root = Path.cwd()
result = (root / \"output\" / \"result.txt\").read_text()
book = openpyxl.load_workbook(root / \"output\" / \"smoke.xlsx\", read_only=True, data_only=True)
sheet = book[\"Smoke\"]
expected = (root / \"input\" / \"toy.txt\").read_text()
assert book.sheetnames == [\"Smoke\"]
assert sheet[\"A1\"].value == \"sandbox-ok\"
assert sheet[\"A2\"].value == expected
assert result == f\"OK\\n{openpyxl.__version__}\\n\"
print(\"verified smoke.xlsx and result.txt\")
PY"
